quote: Garman agrees to indemnify Sparkling and hold it harmless from any and all losses, damages and expenses including without limitation, court costs, arbitration fees, penalties, fines, amounts paid in settlement of claims and reasonable legal fees and expenses of investigation (collectively the "Losses") which Sparkling or any of its respective officers or directors may incur due to a breach of this warranty.
rationale: Garman gives a non-infringement/title warranty backed by an indemnity for our Losses, with the usual procure/modify/replace remedies, and Section 15 expressly places Section 13 outside the liability limitation, so the indemnity is not capped or gutted. No reciprocal indemnity is imposed on us. This sits at the fallback: we note (not flag) the absence of express defence/settlement-control mechanics, the lack of a refund remedy, and the tight 10-day claim-notice requirement, which we would prefer to relax to "prompt written notice".

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We are content for Garman to own its Software, but we cannot have our own data, or the Modifications built for us, vest in Garman without a broad licence back. We have added a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a perpetual, royalty-free licence to use and modify the Improvements and Modifications for our business.

ops.text: Sparkling retains all right, title and interest in and to Sparkling's data (including data converted under Section 4) and Sparkling's Confidential Information, and nothing in this Agreement transfers or assigns any such right to Garman. Garman grants Sparkling a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, reproduce and modify the Improvements and Modifications, on the terms of Section 2, for Sparkling's internal business purposes.

proposal.summary: Confirm Sparkling owns its data and gets a broad licence to Modifications/Improvements

quote: Garman is the owner of all intellectual property rights in the Work (including any Improvements or Modifications thereto), including all related materials, logos, and names provided pursuant to the terms of this Agreement.
rationale: Garman owning its base Software is acceptable, but Section 13 also vests ownership of the Modifications and Improvements — including the Schedule "D" Modifications built for us — in Garman, while the only licence back (Section 2) is a non-transferable, non-exclusive right to use the "Software" at Authorized Locations with no right to modify or sublicense, and the Agreement is silent on ownership of Sparkling's data (including data converted under Section 4). That falls short of the fallback licence-back. We added a Sparkling data-ownership sentence and a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence covering Improvements and Modifications.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 15 excludes indirect damages but sets no monetary cap, so direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties. We have added our standard mutual cap of the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, and kept the indemnity, confidentiality, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP-infringement claims outside the cap.

ops.newText: Except for Excluded Claims, each party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Sparkling under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000. The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to Excluded Claims, meaning a party's breach of Sections 13 or 14, its indemnification obligations, its gross negligence, wilful misconduct or fraud, and its infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights. Sparkling's obligation to pay fees due under this Agreement shall not be treated as damages for the purposes of this Section 15.
ops.oldText: The limitation of liability in this Section 15 shall not apply to breaches of Sections 13 and 14.

proposal.summary: Add a mutual monetary cap with express carve-outs

quote: The exclusive remedy of either party in a claim against the other under this Agreement shall be the recovery of its direct damages. In no event shall either party be liable to the other for the recovery of any special, indirect or consequential damages
rationale: Section 15 is mutual and excludes indirect/consequential damages, and it carves out Sections 13 (IP indemnity) and 14 (confidentiality), but it contains no monetary cap at all — direct-damages exposure is unlimited for both parties, so it fails the fallback requirement of a mutual cap of 12 months' fees. We added the mutual greater-of cap (12 months' fees / USD 1,000,000), expanded the carve-outs to gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement, and confirmed our fee obligations are not "damages".
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs

proposal.comment: [Playbook] A blanket assignment bar with no M&A carve-out is not something we can accept. We have added the affiliate and successor carve-out for Sparkling and made consent for other assignments subject to a reasonableness standard.

ops.newText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed; provided that Sparkling may assign this Agreement, without consent, to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and no such transaction or change of control of Sparkling shall give Garman any right to terminate or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Sparkling and a reasonableness standard

quote: (d) Neither party may assign this Agreement or any rights and obligations under this Agreement to any third party without the written consent of the other party.
rationale: Section 20(d) (reinforced by the Section 3(c) transfer bar) is a blanket consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A/successor carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard, which is walk-away territory under our playbook. We added the affiliate/successor carve-out for Sparkling, a "not unreasonably withheld" standard for other assignments, and confirmed a change of control of Sparkling gives Garman no termination or re-pricing right.

quote: a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
rationale: No exclusivity, sole-source or "all requirements" obligation binds Sparkling; the only use of "exclusive" is the non-exclusive licence grant and the non-exclusive jurisdiction clause. We remain free to buy from other suppliers (Schedule A was not provided, so we will confirm no sole-source language sits in the Fee Schedule).

quote: Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: No liquidated damages, penalties, stipulated sums, late-payment interest or early-termination charges are payable by Sparkling; our convenience termination carries no fee, and the only money-back mechanic runs to us (refund of fees for services not yet rendered on Garman's default, and full refund on rejection under Section 8). Nothing to redline (Schedule A not provided).
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

quote: Garman hereby grants to Sparkling, for the use of Sparkling and affiliated companies of Sparkling operating at Authorized Locations, a non-transferable and non-exclusive licence to use
rationale: The grant expressly covers Sparkling's affiliated companies (no notice condition), is not revocable at Garman's discretion — it runs perpetually while fees are paid and can only fall away on termination under Section 17 — and the escrow licence in Section 16(b) is perpetual and fully paid. This meets the fallback. We note that contractors acting on our behalf are not named and the licence is non-transferable; transferability to a successor is addressed in our assignment redline rather than flagged twice here.

quote: (g) not use the Work to act as a service bureau in whole or in part, for any other Person, except for any affiliate of Sparkling operating at the Authorized Locations.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restraint binds Sparkling's business. Section 3 contains only ordinary software use restrictions (no service-bureau use of Garman's own Software), which do not restrict what businesses we operate or what products we may buy or build.

quote: (b) Sparkling may terminate this Agreement at any time upon ninety (90) calendar days written notice to Garman.
rationale: Sparkling has an unqualified convenience right on 90 days' notice with no early-termination fee or penalty, and Garman has no convenience right at all (it may terminate only for insolvency or uncured material default). This sits at the fallback (90 rather than 30 days); we note only that there is no express pro-rata refund of prepaid maintenance fees on a convenience exit, which we would add if the document is reopened.

quote: provided that Sparkling may itself or by retaining independent experts, examine and test the materials for compliance with the obligations of Garman hereunder
rationale: The Agreement grants Garman no audit, inspection, verification or system-access right against Sparkling; the only examination right runs in our favour (testing the escrowed Codes). Nothing to redline — the absence of any audit right on us is better than our preferred position.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Our accepted governing laws are New York, Delaware, California or England and Wales, so we have moved this to New York law and the New York County courts; Delaware, California or England and Wales would also work if that is easier for you.

ops.newText: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
ops.oldText: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.

proposal.summary: Move governing law and venue to New York

quote: (h) This Agreement shall be governed by the laws of Nova Scotia and the laws of Canada applicable in Nova Scotia. All disputes under this Agreement shall be subject to the non-exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of Nova Scotia.
rationale: Nova Scotia law and courts are outside our accepted list (New York preferred; Delaware, California or England and Wales as fallback), so the clause fails both positions. It is not walk-away territory — venue is non-exclusive and Nova Scotia is our own home province rather than Garman's (Saskatchewan) — so this is a low-heat point: we have proposed New York and will accept any name on the accepted list.

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: There is no most-favoured-nation language anywhere in the Agreement, and in particular no obligation on Sparkling to extend Garman terms as good as those given to third parties. Nothing to redline (Schedule A pricing was not provided and will be checked for MFN language).

quote: Sparkling shall pay the fees as set out in the Fee Schedule in accordance with the terms of this Agreement and the Fee Schedule.
rationale: The body of the Agreement imposes no minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or committed-volume obligation on Sparkling: fees are as set out in the Fee Schedule, maintenance runs in one-year renewable terms, and we may exit on 90 days' notice without penalty. Schedule "A" was not provided, so we will confirm no minimum licence counts or committed maintenance years appear there.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept a no-hire covering all of the other party's employees. We have narrowed Section 19 to a mutual non-solicitation of personnel directly involved in the services, for 12 months from the end of their involvement, with the usual carve-outs for general advertising and unsolicited approaches.

ops.newText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year after the end of an individual's involvement in the provision of services under this Agreement, neither party shall actively solicit for employment any employee of the other party who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement. This Section does not restrict either party from hiring any person, and does not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically directed at the other party's personnel, or to responses to or approaches from any individual made on his or her own initiative.
ops.oldText: During the term of this Agreement and for a period of one year thereafter, both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement.

proposal.summary: Convert the mutual no-hire into a narrow 12-month non-solicit with carve-outs

quote: both parties agree not to hire or allow its respective affiliates to hire any employee of the other party, or any person who was an employee of the other party during the previous six months and who was directly involved in the provision of services under this Agreement
rationale: This is a no-hire, not a non-solicit, and on its face it captures "any employee of the other party" rather than only personnel involved in the services, with no carve-out for general advertising or unsolicited approaches — no-hire provisions are walk-away territory under our playbook. We narrowed it to a mutual 12-month non-solicitation of directly involved personnel with the standard carve-outs; mutuality is preserved.

quote: For a renewable one-year term commencing upon the Maintenance Commencement Date, subject to payment of maintenance fees in accordance with the Fee Schedule but without additional fees or charges, Garman shall provide the following Maintenance Services
rationale: There is no automatic renewal and no non-renewal notice window: the licence is perpetual while fees are paid and maintenance runs in renewable one-year terms, i.e. renewal is effectively by agreement and payment, which meets the preferred position. We note only that no cap on renewal-year maintenance price increases appears in the body of the Agreement (Schedule A not provided); we would add a CPI/3% cap if reopened.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Termination currently obliges us to return the Software but says nothing about getting our own data back or about migration help. We have added transition assistance for up to six months at then-current rates and return of our data within 30 days in a machine-readable format, followed by certified deletion.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement for any reason, Garman shall (i) at Sparkling's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Garman's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) calendar days, return all Sparkling data in its possession or control in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such data from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data-return obligation on termination

quote: Sparkling shall cease using the Software at the end of the ninety (90) day notice period, and shall certify to Garman within thirty (30) calendar days of termination that Sparkling has destroyed or has returned to Garman all Software, Documentation and Codes.
rationale: Termination obligations run one way: we must stop using and return the Software, but there is no transition assistance, no return or export of Sparkling's data (including converted data held in Garman's possession) and no deletion certification. Source-code escrow (Section 16) gives continuity of the Software only, not an exit path. We inserted a Section 17(d) with six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, data return in machine-readable form within 30 days and certified deletion (90 days' assistance is our fallback).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

quote: For the acceptance period and for a period of one year from the Maintenance Commencement Date, and thereafter for as long as the Software is covered by Maintenance Services and is used by Sparkling in accordance with this Agreement, Garman warrants that the Software shall perform in conformance with the Specifications in all material respects.
rationale: The conformance warranty runs for a full year from the Maintenance Commencement Date and continues while maintenance is in place, exceeding our preferred 12-month software period, and there is no "AS IS" disclaimer swallowing it. Real remedies exist: best-efforts repair at no charge (Section 10(c)), rejection with full refund during acceptance (Sections 7–8), and refund of fees for services not rendered on termination for Garman's default. We note only the absence of an express "professional and workmanlike"/compliance-with-laws warranty for the on-site services.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The Agreement has no insurance covenant even though Garman's personnel work on our sites and handle our data. We have added our standard limits (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M is our fallback if the higher limits are a problem).

ops.text: (k) Garman shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Garman processes Sparkling data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Garman shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

quote: (j) This Agreement constitutes the entire Agreement between the parties with respect to its subject matter, and this Agreement supersedes all prior understandings, representations, negotiations and communications between the parties, oral and written.
rationale: The Agreement contains no insurance covenant anywhere, yet Garman's personnel install, convert our data and train on site (Sections 4, 5 and 9). We inserted our standard short insurance paragraph as Section 20(k) (CGL 1M/2M, E&O 2M, cyber 5M where our data is processed, certificates on request), with E&O 1M / cyber 2M available as a fallback.
